test_cases.scenario: Clicking the SAML sign-in button redirects the browser to the IdP SSO URL
test_cases.steps: Navigate to /login/. Click the SAML sign-in button.
test_cases.expected: Browser is redirected to the configured IdP SSO URL (HTTP-Redirect binding).

test_cases.scenario: Redirect URL contains a SAMLRequest parameter
test_cases.steps: Click the SAML sign-in button. Observe the IdP redirect URL.
test_cases.expected: A SAMLRequest query parameter is present in the redirect URL.

test_cases.scenario: Button shows a loading or disabled state while the redirect is being prepared
test_cases.steps: Click the SAML sign-in button. Observe the button immediately after clicking.
test_cases.expected: Button is disabled or shows a loading indicator to prevent double-clicks.

test_cases.scenario: Relay state is forwarded to the IdP when a post-login redirect target is set
test_cases.steps: Navigate to a protected page (e.g. /dashboard/) while unauthenticated. Be redirected to /login/. Click SAML sign-in.
test_cases.expected: The relay state containing the originally requested URL is included in the redirect to the IdP.

test_cases.scenario: Completing SAML login at the IdP logs the user into the app
test_cases.steps: Navigate to /login/. Click the SAML sign-in button. Authenticate at the IdP.
test_cases.expected: User is authenticated. Browser returns to the app with a valid session.

test_cases.scenario: User is redirected to the application after successful SAML login
test_cases.steps: Complete the full SAML authentication flow at the IdP.
test_cases.expected: Browser lands on the main app page (e.g. dashboard). No login page is shown again.

test_cases.scenario: Session is active after successful SAML login
test_cases.steps: Complete SAML login. Navigate to a protected route.
test_cases.expected: Protected route loads correctly. User is not redirected back to /login/.

test_cases.scenario: User's email from the SAML assertion is stored on the account
test_cases.steps: Complete SAML login with a user whose IdP email is 'saml@example.com'. Check the logged-in user's profile.
test_cases.expected: App stores and displays 'saml@example.com' as the authenticated user's email.

test_cases.scenario: User's first and last name from SAML attributes are applied to the account
test_cases.steps: Complete SAML login with an IdP that returns first_name and last_name attributes. Check the user profile.
test_cases.expected: First name and last name in the app reflect the values from the SAML assertion.

test_cases.scenario: Relay state is honoured — user lands on the originally requested page after login
test_cases.steps: Attempt to access /dashboard/ while unauthenticated. Log in via SAML.
test_cases.expected: After successful login, browser lands on /dashboard/ (not the generic home page).

test_cases.scenario: Missing SAMLResponse in the ACS POST shows an error to the user
test_cases.steps: Navigate to the ACS URL directly without a SAMLResponse parameter.
test_cases.expected: App displays an error message. User is not logged in.

test_cases.scenario: Tampered or invalid SAMLResponse signature shows an error
test_cases.steps: Intercept the SAMLResponse from the IdP. Modify its content before it reaches the ACS. Submit the tampered response.
test_cases.expected: App rejects the assertion. An error is shown to the user. No session is created.

test_cases.scenario: SAML authentication failure status from the IdP shows an error
test_cases.steps: Trigger an IdP-side authentication failure (e.g. wrong credentials). IdP posts a failure SAMLResponse to ACS.
test_cases.expected: App shows a clear error message. User is not logged in.

test_cases.scenario: SAMLResponse from an unknown IdP entity ID shows an error
test_cases.steps: Submit a SAMLResponse whose Issuer does not match any configured SAML provider.
test_cases.expected: App displays an error. No session is created.

test_cases.scenario: SAMLResponse with a missing NameID shows an error
test_cases.steps: Submit a SAMLResponse that contains no NameID element in the Assertion.
test_cases.expected: App displays an error. User is not logged in.

test_cases.scenario: Error message is user-friendly and does not expose internal details
test_cases.steps: Trigger a SAML error (e.g. invalid signature). Inspect the error message shown.
test_cases.expected: Message is readable. No stack traces, raw XML, or internal exception messages are visible.

test_cases.scenario: Error page provides a way to return to the login page and retry
test_cases.steps: Encounter a SAML error. Observe the error page.
test_cases.expected: A link or button to return to /login/ is available.

test_cases.scenario: Replaying a SAMLResponse that has already been used shows an error or starts a fresh session
test_cases.steps: Capture a valid SAMLResponse from a successful login. Resubmit the same SAMLResponse to the ACS URL.
test_cases.expected: App either rejects the replay (preferred) or creates a fresh valid session. No silent privilege escalation.

test_cases.scenario: First-time SAML login creates a new user account
test_cases.steps: Complete SAML login with an email address that has no existing account in the app.
test_cases.expected: A new user account is created. User lands on the app. Account email matches the SAML NameID.

test_cases.scenario: Returning SAML user is not duplicated on subsequent logins
test_cases.steps: Complete SAML login twice with the same IdP account.
test_cases.expected: Same user account is used both times. Only one account exists for that email.

test_cases.scenario: SAML user cannot log in using classic email/password credentials
test_cases.steps: Create an account via SAML login. Switch AUTH_MODE to classic. Attempt to log in with the same email and any password.
test_cases.expected: Login fails. No password is set on SAML-created accounts.

test_cases.scenario: User profile reflects name attributes received from the IdP
test_cases.steps: Complete SAML login with an IdP returning first_name='Alice', last_name='Smith'. Visit the user profile.
test_cases.expected: Profile shows first name 'Alice' and last name 'Smith'.

test_cases.scenario: SAML login button is reachable and activatable via keyboard
test_cases.steps: Navigate to /login/ in SAML mode. Press Tab to focus the sign-in button. Press Enter.
test_cases.expected: Focus lands on the button. Pressing Enter initiates the SAML redirect.

test_cases.scenario: SAML login button has a visible focus ring
test_cases.steps: Tab to the SAML sign-in button on /login/.
test_cases.expected: A visible focus indicator (outline or highlight) is present on the button.

test_cases.scenario: Login page with SAML mode is usable on mobile (375px)
test_cases.steps: Open /login/ at 375px viewport width with AUTH_MODE=saml.
test_cases.expected: SAML button is fully visible and tappable. No horizontal scroll. No content overflow.

test_cases.scenario: Login page with SAML mode is usable on tablet (768px)
test_cases.steps: Open /login/ at 768px viewport with SAML mode.
test_cases.expected: Layout adapts correctly. Button and branding remain usable.

test_cases.scenario: SAMLResponse content is never exposed in any frontend page or URL
test_cases.steps: Complete a SAML login flow. Inspect all browser URLs, page source, and network responses visible to the frontend.
test_cases.expected: The raw SAMLResponse XML or base64 content is only ever in the ACS POST body — never rendered in the page or URL bar.

test_cases.scenario: IdP X.509 certificate is not exposed in any frontend response
test_cases.steps: Navigate to /login/ and initiate SAML. Inspect all network responses from the app.
test_cases.expected: The stored IdP certificate does not appear in any page source or API response visible to the browser.

test_cases.scenario: Dark mode applies correctly to the SAML login page
test_cases.steps: Toggle to dark mode. Navigate to /login/ with SAML mode.
test_cases.expected: All elements use the dark theme. No light-mode remnants visible.

test_cases.scenario: SAML login page loads within 2 seconds on local dev
test_cases.steps: Open DevTools Network tab. Navigate to /login/ with SAML mode.
test_cases.expected: DOM interactive within 2 seconds on local network.
